title: What hallmarking is
content: The BIS Hallmarking FAQ states: "Hallmarking is the accurate determination and official recording of the proportionate content of precious metal in precious metal articles." BIS says it protects consumers against malpractice and helps develop India's export competitiveness.

title: Which metals are hallmarked in India
content: According to the BIS Hallmarking FAQ, gold and silver are currently hallmarked in India, under IS 1417:2016 (gold) and IS 2112:2014 (silver), along with the related testing standards IS 1418:2009 and IS 2113:2014. Individual records for these standards are in the indian_standards category.

title: The three marks that make up a hallmark
content: The BIS Hallmarking FAQ states: "Since the introduction of HUID (i.e. 1st July 2021) hallmark consists of 3 marks viz, BIS logo, purity of the article in caratage as well as fineness and six-digit alphanumeric HUID number."

title: What HUID means
content: HUID stands for Hallmark Unique Identification. The BIS Hallmarking FAQ states: "It is a six-digit alphanumeric number which is unique for each hallmarked item and is traceable. Customer can also verify the HUID number in the BIS Care App using the 'Verify HUID' feature."

title: Gold purity grades permitted for hallmarking
content: The BIS Hallmarking FAQ states: "IS 1417:2016 permits hallmarking of six caratage (fineness in ppt) of gold jewellery/artefacts, viz. 14K(585), 18K(750), 20K(833), 22K(916), 23K(958) and 24KS(995)." (The FAQ prints the last grade as 24KS.) So the permitted gold caratages for hallmarking are 14K (585), 18K (750), 20K (833), 22K (916), 23K (958) and 24K (995) parts-per-thousand fineness.

title: Silver purity grades permitted for hallmarking
content: The BIS Hallmarking FAQ states: "IS 2112 : 2014 permits hallmarking of of six grades(fineness in ppt) of silver jewellery/artefacts, viz. 800(800.0), 835(835.0), 900(900.0), 925(925.0), 970(970.0) and 990(990.0)" (quoted as printed).

title: Hallmarking charges for gold and silver articles
content: According to the BIS Hallmarking FAQ, hallmarking charges are Rs. 45 per article for gold (minimum Rs. 200 per consignment) and Rs. 35 per article for silver (minimum Rs. 150 per consignment), with applicable service tax and other levies extra.

title: Mandatory hallmarking of gold jewellery and artefacts
content: BIS states that mandatory hallmarking of gold jewellery and gold artefacts is governed by the Hallmarking of Gold Jewellery and Gold Artefacts Order, 2020, and became effective on 23 June 2021. It has been rolled out in phases and progressively extended to additional districts. The order applies to gold in 14, 18, 20, 22, 23 and 24 carat purities.
document_name: BIS: Mandatory hallmarking of Gold jewellery/artefacts

title: Exemptions from mandatory hallmarking
content: According to BIS, exemptions from mandatory hallmarking include jewellers with an annual turnover up to Rs. 40 lakh, gold jewellery meant for export and re-import as per trade policy, and certain other categories specified under the Quality Control Order. Details are set out in the order and its amendments.
document_name: BIS: Mandatory hallmarking of Gold jewellery/artefacts

title: Jeweller registration with BIS is free and valid for lifetime
content: The BIS jewellers page states that a jeweller applies for registration online (through the National Single Window System portal or manakonline.in) and that "the certificate of registration is granted instantly without the need to pay any fees and the same stands valid for lifetime."

title: Which jewellers must register with BIS
content: The BIS jewellers page states that any manufacturer, wholesaler, distributor or retailer engaged in selling hallmarked precious metal (gold/silver) articles has to mandatorily get registered with BIS. It also notes that artisans doing job work may be exempted and that jewellers with an annual turnover up to Rs. 40 lakh are not mandatorily required to register.

title: Obligations of a BIS-registered jeweller
content: According to BIS, a registered jeweller must get articles hallmarked, ensure the bill/invoice includes item description, net weight, purity in carat and fineness, and hallmarking charges, keep a 10x magnification glass available so a customer can see the hallmark, and cooperate with BIS surveillance officers collecting samples.

title: How a consumer can check a hallmark
content: According to the BIS Hallmarking FAQ, a consumer can verify the six-digit HUID number of a hallmarked article using the BIS Care App. Each article in a pair and every detachable part must carry its own HUID. Jewellers are required to have a 10x magnification glass so customers can view the hallmark.
